questions.q: Where did Alan and David sleep at the Heugh of Corrynakiegh?
choices: In a shallow cave on a bed of heather
In a shepherd's hut beside the burn
Under a pine tree wrapped in plaids
In a hollow on top of two great rocks
questions.evidence: We slept in the cave, making our bed of heather bushes

questions.q: They spent their days at the water-side, "groping about or (as they say) guddling" for trout. What is "guddling"?
choices: Catching fish with your bare hands
Fishing with a rod and a fly
Spearing fish with a sharp stick
Trapping fish in a woven basket
questions.evidence: the little trouts that we caught with our hands under the stones

questions.q: How did Alan behave while teaching David to use a sword?
choices: He was patient and praised every small step
He stormed and scolded and pushed him very close
He laughed so hard that he could hardly teach
He gave up after the first lesson in disgust
questions.evidence: he stormed at me all through the lessons in a very violent manner of scolding

questions.q: Why does David think Alan was glad to give him sword lessons?
choices: David sometimes beat him at fishing, and Alan was far better at swords
Alan was afraid that soldiers would soon find them in the cave
Alan had promised James that he would teach David
Alan needed practice himself after so long at sea
questions.evidence: as I had sometimes the upper-hand of him in the fishing

questions.q: What did Alan make to send as a signal to his friend John Breck Maccoll?
choices: A small wooden cross with blackened ends
A tartan flag tied to a long pole
A letter written on birch bark
A ring of stones in front of the house
questions.evidence: he fashioned it in a cross, the four ends of which he blackened on the coals

questions.q: What did Alan tie onto the cross along with the silver button?
choices: A sprig of birch and a sprig of fir
A lock of his hair and a feather
A trout and a bit of oatmeal
A scrap of red cloth and a ribbon
questions.evidence: tying in a little sprig of birch and another of fir

questions.q: What was the button on the cross meant to tell John Breck?
choices: That the son of Duncan Stewart was in the heather and needed him
That the whole clan was to rise up and fight the Campbells
That John Breck should bring the button to James at once
That Alan was leaving for France and would not return
questions.evidence: THE SON OF DUNCAN IS IN THE HEATHER, AND HAS NEED OF ME

questions.q: Why didn't Alan just write John Breck a letter in the first place?
choices: He had no paper
John Breck could not read
Letters might be stolen
He had forgotten how
questions.evidence: it would be a sore job for John Breck to read it

questions.q: What did Alan and David do the day after Alan placed the cross in the window?
choices: Lay at the edge of the wood keeping a close look-out
Went down to the clachan to find John Breck
Moved to a new hiding place farther up the mountain
Fished all day in the burn as if nothing had happened
questions.evidence: we lay the next day in the borders of the wood and kept a close look-out

questions.q: How did Alan guide John Breck to their hiding place?
choices: By whistling to him again and again
By lighting a small fire as a signal
By waving the great-coat from a rock
By sending David down to meet him
questions.evidence: so by the sound of whistling, he was guided to the spot where we lay

questions.q: What did Alan use to write the letter to James?
choices: A dove's quill, gunpowder ink, and a corner of his commission
A burnt stick, and a page torn from David's book
A pen and ink borrowed from the bouman's house
A sharp stone, and a flat piece of birch bark
questions.evidence: found the quill of a cushat-dove, which he shaped into a pen

questions.q: What news did the bouman bring back about James of the Glens?
choices: He had fled to France
He was in prison at Fort William
He had been hanged at Inverara
He was hiding in Mamore
questions.evidence: James and some of his servants were already clapped in prison at Fort William

questions.q: What reward did the bill offer for Alan and David?
choices: Ten pounds
Fifty pounds
One hundred pounds
Five hundred pounds

questions.q: Why did the description of David on the bill make him feel safer instead of more afraid?
choices: It said he was much older than he really was
He had already changed out of the clothes it described
It gave the wrong colour for his hair and eyes
It said that he spoke only the Gaelic tongue
questions.evidence: since I had changed these rags, the description had ceased to be a danger

questions.q: Why would Alan not change out of his fine clothes?
choices: He had no others and would not go to France in a bonnet
He thought no soldier would dare to stop a gentleman
He had promised his father never to wear Lowland clothes
He believed the bill described someone else entirely
questions.evidence: A fine sight I would be, if I went back to France in a bonnet!

questions.q: What did David privately think, but not say, after seeing the bill?
choices: That he would be safer apart from Alan
That Alan had truly fired the shot
That James had betrayed them both
That he should give himself up
questions.evidence: if I were to separate from Alan and his tell-tale clothes I should be safe against arrest

questions.q: What happened when Alan asked John Breck for his button back?
choices: The bouman said he had lost it, then suddenly found it
The bouman said James had kept it as a keepsake
The bouman refused to give it back without more money
The bouman said soldiers had taken it from him
questions.evidence: he seemed to find that button and handed it to Alan

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Alan and David hiding in Corrynakiegh while getting money sent from James
Alan and David being chased out of Corrynakiegh by soldiers
David learning to fish and deciding to live in the Highlands
John Breck leading the soldiers to Alan and David's cave
questions.evidence: we must get word sent to James, and he must find the siller for us
